candidates.name: AirBnB_Occupancy
candidates.what_it_holds: Implements the classic 'San Francisco Budget & Legislative Analyst's Office' review-based occupancy methodology (review rate 30.5%-72%, midpoint 50%, used to convert Inside Airbnb review counts into estimated bookings, x avg length-of-stay per city, capped at 70% occupancy) and proposes a refinement: filters to multi-listing hosts (20+ properties), 365-day-available, Instant-Book-enabled listings (calendar more likely accurate), then scrapes Airbnb's live calendar API for a subset to validate/calibrate against the review-based estimate. Built on Inside Airbnb listings+reviews as the base dataset. No large committed data files found (methodology/code repo, some scraped calendar snapshots for validation).
candidates.why_useful: Directly the 'San Francisco model' / review-to-booking-ratio occupancy estimator named in the theme; addresses gap #2 (realised occupancy for STRs from a free source) — gives a concrete, reproducible formula (review rate x ALOS, city-level) we could re-run on our own 123-market Inside Airbnb panel to get an independent occupancy/nights proxy, and the Instant-Book calendar-accuracy filter is a usable refinement for cross-checking Inside Airbnb calendar-derived occupancy.
candidates.geography: Not city-specific in the base method; validation touches at least one city (methodology generalizable to any Inside Airbnb market)
candidates.time_coverage: Not specified (uses whatever Inside Airbnb vintage is pulled)
candidates.size_hint: small code repo, methodology + some scraped validation data

candidates.name: Airbnb-Dynamic-Pricing-Optimization
candidates.what_it_holds: San-Francisco-only project (Bayview, Chinatown, etc.) that clusters Inside Airbnb listings within a 3-mile radius and fits regression (poly/linear) demand curves relating price to occupancy; explicitly assumes review rate = 0.5 as the constant to convert reviews to estimated bookings (same 'SF model' family as edmondodriscoll's repo). Also pulls SF police incident (crime) data as a covariate. Uses InsideAirbnb as the listings source; no confirmation of large committed CSVs beyond notebooks.
candidates.why_useful: A second independent implementation of the same review-rate occupancy-estimation convention, with a neighborhood-cluster demand-curve method (price vs. occupancy) that could be repurposed as a cross-check method for nights/occupancy estimation on our Inside Airbnb panel; the SF crime-data-as-demand-covariate angle is a minor bonus but not central to ABNB forecasting.

candidates.name: airdna (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Not a data repo — a third-party documentation/OpenAPI profile of the commercial AirDNA Enterprise API (market metrics, STR listing data, comparable-property sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates, occupancy/ADR/RevPAR/booking-lead-time/length-of-stay time series across 10M+ listings, 120k+ markets). Contains an OpenAPI spec, APIs.yml, Postman/Open API collections, and pricing/rate-limit metadata; explicitly 'no software, no data' — a map of what AirDNA's paid API exposes, not the data itself. Points to https://www.airdna.co (paid).
candidates.why_useful: Confirms exactly which realised-occupancy/ADR/booking-lead-time fields AirDNA sells (gap #2 and #3 candidate vendor), which is useful for scoping a potential paid-data ask, but yields nothing free or committed; low direct research value on its own.

candidates.name: airbnb_victoria
candidates.what_it_holds: Inside Airbnb pull for a 'Victoria' market (city name unconfirmed as Melbourne/Victoria AU vs. Victoria BC/Victoria TX from the fetched README alone) with the standard three files committed/generated: listings.csv (all listing features), calendar.csv (daily calendar/availability per listing), reviews.csv (detailed reviews). Analysis in pandas/plotnine/sklearn.
candidates.why_useful: One more single-city Inside Airbnb calendar+reviews snapshot; only worth flagging if the vintage is older or the city sits outside our current 13+120-market coverage — needs a follow-up city/date confirmation before treating as new coverage.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: possible duplicate of existing Inside Airbnb holdings if same city/vintage as what we already hold

candidates.name: inside-airbnb-tutorial
candidates.category_note: academic/teaching tooling for pulling Inside Airbnb data on a schedule
candidates.what_it_holds: Tilburg Science Hub tutorial/pipeline for pulling Inside Airbnb's monthly-updated calendar.csv and listings.csv programmatically (documented ETL steps rather than a one-off notebook).
candidates.why_useful: A maintained, documented pull method (vs. ad hoc scripts) for Inside Airbnb calendar/listings data that could be adapted into our own point-in-time capture pipeline to get monthly vintages before the CDN drops them (addresses part of gap #1's forward-looking side: capturing dumps before they age off).

candidates.name: Travel-Agency-Database
candidates.what_it_holds: ETL project that downloads calendar.csv.gz directly from the Inside Airbnb CDN and combines it with other travel/forecast data into a database.
candidates.why_useful: Another working, scriptable one-command pull of Inside Airbnb calendar.csv.gz; marginal beyond what our team's own capture scripts already do, but confirms a clean download pattern and could be scavenged for a robust retry/URL-pattern implementation.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicates our existing Inside Airbnb capture tooling

notes: Hard-capped at 6 gh search calls per instructions; all six (airbnb occupancy estimate / airbnb calendar availability / san francisco model airbnb / airbnb scraper calendar / inside airbnb archive historical / topic:airbnb-data) returned almost nothing useful — GitHub's code search index for 'airbnb' is dominated by Airbnb-clone bootcamp apps, scraper-as-a-service ads (Apify/Oxylabs/omkarcloud), and single-city Kaggle-style EDA notebooks; none of the six calls surfaced a genuine calendar/occupancy dataset repo. Switched to WebSearch (site:github.com and keyword queries) which found the two 'review-rate' occupancy-model repos (edmondodriscoll, tule2236) that both implement the same San Francisco Budget & Legislative Analyst's Office methodology (review rate 30.5-72%, midpoint 50%, x average length of stay, capped at 70% occupancy) that Inside Airbnb itself documents at insideairbnb.com/data-assumptions — worth noting Inside Airbnb's own site explains this exact methodology, so the GitHub value-add is working code, not a new idea. Did not find: any GitHub mirror of pre-2023 historical Inside Airbnb dumps, any free/leaked AirDNA-style realised-occupancy export, any booking-lead-time/cancellation dataset specific to STRs (only generic Kaggle hotel-booking-demand cancellation datasets, which are hotel not STR and already adjacent to what we hold via the Portugal hotel dataset). No rate-limit errors encountered on gh CLI. Suggest a future scout specifically target 'Quattrone airbnb occupancy' (academic paper with a companion repo estimating true occupancy from reviews using a Poisson process, a more rigorous alternative to the flat review-rate assumption) and 'AirbnbHackathon' / city open-data portals (e.g., SF OSTR, LA HSO) for any committed calendar-derived occupancy tables, since those may sit under the regulatory theme rather than this one.
